newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares jump as bank leads A market rally.
newsitem.headline: China B shares jump as bank leads A market rally.

text.p: China's B share indices jumped ahead on Friday, pulled up by skyrocketing domestic currency A markets that were boosted in turn by the return of the punished Shenzhen Development Bank to trading, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index rose 1.822 points, or 2.19 percent, to close at 85.047 while the Shenzhen B share market ended up 2.52 points, or 1.72 percent, at 149.15.
"The main reason for the gain was the strong performance of the A share markets," said one broker.
"The Shenzhen Development Bank sparked the Shenzhen A market rally, which then helped the Shanghai A market," said another broker.
Shenzhen's A share index rose 28.37 points, or 6.73 percent, to 449.97 points while Shanghai's A market leaped 64.136 points, or 4.99 percent, to close at 1,349.150.
Shenzhen Development Bank Co, returning to trade on Friday after a five-day suspension as punishment for illegal trading, closed at its 10 percent limit up of 33.96 points.

"Today's bull run was led by heavyweight Shenzhen Development Bank, whose surprisingly strong performance underpinned investor confidence and sparked a wave of buying in a range of shares," said Cheng Li, an analyst at China Guotai Securities.
Last week, Chinese securities authorities sacked the bank's president and confiscated nearly 100 million yuan the firm had made from speculating in its own shares.
Beijing last week also punished a string of listed firms and brokerages for trading irregularities as part of a drive to cool the heated markets.
"Investors scrambled to buy the bank shares due to confidence in the company's earning prospects," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.

The bank, a market leader due to its large capitalisation and robust earnings record, led a bull run in Shenzhen between January and May this year before its share price fell due to the official investigation into its trading practices.
Brokers also said investors poured funds into A shares in the expectation of sustained rises in the final days before the Hong Kong handover at midnight on June 30.
The A and B share markets might see smaller rises early next week, brokers said.
"A new run cannot start without fresh capital but the market will move forward a little if there is no negative news over the weekend," one broker said.
The biggest gainer in the Shanghai B market was Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Device Co Ltd, which soared $0.018, or 9.00 percent, $0.218.
In Shenzhen's B share market, Chengming Paper put in the strongest performance, rising HK$0.46 or 7.08 percent, to HK$6.96.
